clean_source_blocks.text: Kem Sokha was serving a 27-year sentence on treason charges, which were widely derided as politically motivated. Cambodia's ​former opposition leader Kem Sokha, who was serving a 27-year sentence for treason, has been pardoned, the country's former prime minister said. Hun Sen, ​who is currently Cambodia's acting head of state, signed a decree pardoning his political rival on behalf of King Norodom Sihamoni. Sokha, the former leader of the now-dissolved Cambodian National Rescue Party (CNRP), was first arrested in 2017 over a video where he said he had received support from US pro-democracy groups. He has been held under house arrest since he was found guilty of treason in 2023. The charges have been widely derided as politically motivated by human rights groups.

Cambodia's ​former opposition leader Kem Sokha, who was serving a 27-year sentence for treason, has been pardoned, the country's former prime minister said. Hun Sen, ​who is currently Cambodia's acting head of state, signed a decree pardoning his political rival on behalf of King Norodom Sihamoni. Sokha, the former leader of the now-dissolved Cambodian National Rescue Party (CNRP), was first arrested in 2017 over a video where he said he had received support from US pro-democracy groups. He has been held under house arrest since he was found guilty of treason in 2023. The charges have been widely derided as politically motivated by human rights groups. Hun Sen posted on Facebook that Sokha had been "pardoned", alongside a photo of the royal decree signed by him.
Kem Sokha was serving a 27-year sentence on treason charges, which were widely derided as politically motivated.

Many political opponents were convicted during Hun Sen’s time in power while Kem Sokha’s CNRP co-founder Sam Rainsy remains in self-exile in France Cambodia’s acting head of state, former prime minister Hun Sen, pardoned opposition leader Kem Sokha on Monday from a sentence of almost three decades for treason. Kem Sokha, who was convicted of trying to topple the former long-ruling leader’s government and sentenced to 27 years, “is pardoned”, Hun Sen posted on social media alongside a royal decree signed by him. Hun Sen, who ruled Cambodia for nearly four decades, stepped down as prime minister in 2023 and handed power to his eldest son, Hun Manet. But Hun Sen is still president of the Senate, remains an influential figure in national politics, and is acting head of state while King Norodom Sihamoni receives medical treatment abroad.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Cambodia's ​former opposition leader Kem Sokha, who was serving a 27-year sentence for treason, has been pardoned, the country's former prime minister said.

Hun Sen, ​who is currently Cambodia's acting head of state, signed a decree pardoning his political rival on behalf of King Norodom Sihamoni.

Sokha, the former leader of the now-dissolved Cambodian National Rescue Party (CNRP), was first arrested in 2017 over a video where he said he had received support from US pro-democracy groups.

He has been held under house arrest since he was found guilty of treason in 2023. The charges have been widely derided as politically motivated by human rights groups.

Hun Sen posted on Facebook that Sokha had been "pardoned", alongside a photo of the royal decree signed by him.

His son, Hun Manet, who took over as prime minister from his father in 2023, said the pardon was "one more step towards strengthening national unity".

It came after an appeal against Sokha's sentence was rejected last month. But it did not include overturning a ban on the politician leaving Cambodia for five years.

Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch, said: "Hun Sen's decision to pardon Kem Sokha after more than eight years in arbitrary detention partially reverses a grievous injustice, but it is deplorable that Sokha remains barred from participating in politics or leaving the country.

"Cambodia's remaining opposition politicians and parties are still under constant threat of arbitrary arrest and baseless restrictions. The government needs to ensure that political rights are respected in the country."

Sokha's CNRP party came close to securing a shock victory in the 2013 general election over Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) despite accusations of vote-rigging and intimidation.

As the next election approached, Sokha's party was the only viable threat to Hun Sen's rule.

The opposition leader was arrested in 2017, less than a year ahead of the crucial vote, which the CNRP was eventually banned from contesting, making Cambodia a de facto one-party state.

His arrest coincided with a crackdown on government critics.

On the day of his arrest, the Cambodia Daily published its last ever newspaper as it was shut down amid a crackdown on independent media. It ran a front page headline "Descent Into Outright Dictatorship" above a photo of a startled Sokha in handcuffs.

payload.title: Kambodžan entinen oppositiojohtaja Kem Sokha sai armahduksen
payload.summary: Kambodžan entinen oppositiojohtaja Kem Sokha on armahdettu 27 vuoden maanpetostuomiosta. Ihmisoikeusjärjestöt ovat pitäneet syytteitä laajasti poliittisesti motivoituina.
payload.content:
Kambodžan entinen oppositiojohtaja Kem Sokha on saanut armahduksen 27 vuoden maanpetostuomiosta. Armahduspäätöksestä kertoi maan entinen pääministeri Hun Sen, joka toimii tällä hetkellä Kambodžan virkaatekevänä valtionpäämiehenä kuningas Norodom Sihamonin puolesta.

## Pitkä tuomio ja kotiaresti

Kem Sokha johti aiemmin Cambodian National Rescue Party -oppositiopuoluetta, joka on sittemmin hajotettu. Hänet pidätettiin vuonna 2017 videon perusteella, jolla hän kertoi saaneensa tukea yhdysvaltalaisilta demokratiaa tukevilta ryhmiltä.

Sokha todettiin vuonna 2023 syylliseksi maanpetokseen. Tuomio oli 27 vuotta, ja sen jälkeen häntä on pidetty kotiarestissa. Ihmisoikeusjärjestöt ovat pitäneet syytteitä laajasti poliittisesti motivoituina.

Hun Sen julkaisi sosiaalisessa mediassa tiedon, jonka mukaan Sokha on armahdettu. Julkaisun yhteydessä oli kuva kuninkaallisesta asetuksesta, jonka Hun Sen oli allekirjoittanut kuningas Norodom Sihamonin puolesta.

## Hun Senin vaikutusvalta jatkuu

Hun Sen johti Kambodžaa lähes neljän vuosikymmenen ajan ennen kuin hän väistyi pääministerin tehtävästä vuonna 2023. Vallan siirron jälkeen pääministeriksi nousi hänen vanhin poikansa Hun Manet.

Vaikka Hun Sen ei enää ole pääministeri, hän toimii senaatin puheenjohtajana ja on edelleen keskeinen hahmo Kambodžan politiikassa. Hän toimii nyt myös virkaatekevänä valtionpäämiehenä, koska kuningas Norodom Sihamoni on ulkomailla saamassa lääketieteellistä hoitoa.

Kambodžassa useita Hun Senin poliittisia vastustajia tuomittiin hänen valtakautensa aikana. Kem Sokhan CNRP-puolueen toinen perustaja Sam Rainsy elää yhä maanpaossa Ranskassa. Sokhan armahdus muuttaa hänen henkilökohtaista asemaansa, mutta lähdeaineiston perusteella sen laajemmista poliittisista seurauksista ei ole vielä varmuutta.

Hänet tuomittiin vuonna 2023 ja häntä on pidetty kotiarestissa.
Hun Sen allekirjoitti armahdusasetuksen kuningas Norodom Sihamonin puolesta.
